source_documents.title: 1-Azaazulene constructs: Overcoming the weak fluorescence of azulene derivatives via S1-S0 transitions

reference_evidence_units.quote: 1-azaazulene constructs demonstrate effective S1 -S0 transitions, resulting in enhanced fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-NN, Ph-ON, Py-NN
reference_evidence_units.statement: Unlike azulene (S2 emission), the 1-azaazulene complexes emit from S1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, the reduced S2 -S1 energy separation accelerates the non-radiative S2 → S1 conversion compared to azulene, effectively suppressing the anti-Kasha S2 → S0 radiative transition.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1-azaazulene core
reference_evidence_units.statement: A smaller S2-S1 gap and a wider S0-S1 gap than azulene make the core Kasha-compliant.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast to the anti-Kasha fluorescence observed in azulene derivatives, all four 1-azaazulene constructs display S1 → S0 emission fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-NN, Ph-ON, Py-NN

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, its PLQY is only 0.3 %, likely due to ultrafast nonradiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-NN
reference_evidence_units.statement: Ph-NN: 705 nm emission, PLQY 0.3%, lifetime 0.18 ns.

reference_evidence_units.quote: reveals an exceptionally short luminescence lifetime (τ ) of 0.18 ns for Ph-NN, yielding a radiative transition rate (kr ) of 1.67 × 107 s−1 and a nonradiative rate (knr ) of 5.54 × 109 s−1 (Table 1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-NN

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, Ph-NN and Ca-NN show significantly red-shifted absorption at 597 and 555 nm, accompanied by broader absorption bands lacking distinct shoulders, which suggests excitations with pronounced charge-transfer (CT) characteristics.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-NN
reference_evidence_units.statement: Broad, red-shifted absorption read as CT excitation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Ph-ON and Py-NN display maximum absorption peaks at 487 and 501 nm, respectively, with pronounced shoulder peaks, indicating dominant localized excitations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-ON, Py-NN

reference_evidence_units.quote: Their enhanced PLQYs arise from both increased kr and reduced knr .
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-ON (and Ca-NN)
reference_evidence_units.statement: Ph-ON: PLQY 2.9%, 0.84 ns, kr 3.45e7, knr 1.16e9 s-1 (versus Ph-NN).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Py-NN, incorporating a pyrrole group, achieved a remarkable photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 19.3 % at 560 nm, attributed to enhanced HOMO-LUMO orbital overlap with an oscillator strength (f) of 0.4973, resulting in a high radiative rate (kr = 9.51 × 107 s−1 ) and suppressed non-radiative decay (knr = 0.40 × 109 s−1 ).
reference_evidence_units.subject: Py-NN
reference_evidence_units.statement: Py-NN: PLQY 19.3%, 2.03 ns; the highest kr and lowest knr of the series.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In addition, Py-NN demonstrated a relatively large energy gap (E = 2.75 eV) and smallest reorganization energy (λM = 3942 cm−1 ), which is conducive to decelerating nonradiative decay rate (see Supporting information for details).
reference_evidence_units.subject: Py-NN
reference_evidence_units.statement: Larger gap and smallest reorganization energy slow nonradiative decay.

reference_evidence_units.quote: TD-DFT calculations show that the oscillator strengths (f) for the S0 → S1 transition of Ph-NN, Ph-ON, Ca-NN, and Py-NN are 0.3299, 0.3009, 0.3458, and 0.4973, respectively.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ph-NN, Ph-ON, Py-NN

reference_evidence_units.quote: These pronounced π -π interactions lead to a decrease in the PLQY of the thin films due to aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) effects (Table S5 in Supporting information).
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four complexes
reference_evidence_units.statement: Antiparallel pi-stacking (3.32-3.47 A) in the crystals; film PLQY drops (ACQ).

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Broad red-shifted absorption read as CT excitation.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Pi-stacking in the solid lowers the film PLQY (ACQ).

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: S1 emission at 705 nm with very low PLQY, explained by ultrafast nonradiative decay (knr 5.5e9 s-1 against kr 1.7e7 s-1).
